portion_doctrine: This portion (segs 1-10) is a Claude AI tutorial video transcript. Most content is boilerplate introduction/UI walkthrough with repetitive sales messaging. Real value concentrated in: (1) three-part prompting formula (Instructions-Context-Constraints), (2) mega-prompt generation pattern (ask AI to write better prompts for you), (3) custom instructions persistence, (4) web search integration, (5) project-scoped workspaces with custom instruction isolation, (6) file upload for persistent knowledge, (7) skills/workflows/connectors framework, (8) model selection strategy (Sonnet+extended-thinking as default, Opus for complex), (9) Claude app vs browser differences. Junk-to-gold ratio: 65-70% boilerplate video sales copy, hooks, UI navigation. Extracted only actionable tactics.
operating_rules: 90% of users use AI wrong; specificity beats generality in prompts
Web search must always be enabled for research-oriented tasks
Separate search task from synthesis task; let knowledge inform decisions
Desktop app faster and supports plugins/skills better than browser version
Custom instructions persist across all conversation in a project
File uploads create persistent knowledge base for future references
Extended thinking model helps guide you with follow-up questions vs generic answers
Model selection: Sonnet+extended-thinking as default; Opus for complex/longer tasks; Haiku for quick tasks
Three-part prompt formula required: Instructions (what to do) + Context (full background/data) + Constraints (rules/style/format/length)
Ask Claude at end of prompt to request any missing context from you
Skills = persistent reusable processes saved for repeated tasks
Hooks folder = rules that must always be enforced without asking
Projects are workspaces with isolated custom instructions to maintain context
Connectors allow Claude to pull data from external apps (email, ClickUp, Granola, etc.)
Mega-prompts: Let AI generate more detailed prompts for you instead of writing them manually

prompts: Mega-prompt template: 'Can you create a detailed prompt in order to [task]? Generate me a prompt that will research [domain], find best opportunities and methods that can [outcome]. Do deep research and create a prompt.'

Generic-to-specific example: Instead of 'How do I market my real estate business?' use 'I'm a 30-year-old male in Las Vegas. Create a detailed prompt for viral marketing campaigns in my niche. Research competitors, find best methods, opportunities to explode my business.'
Three-part structure: [INSTRUCTIONS: define what to do] + [CONTEXT: full background/data/examples] + [CONSTRAINTS: rules/style/tone/format/length/examples]
Context-eliciting prompt: Ask Claude 'Are there any missing context or details I should provide to improve this answer?'
Ground-first pattern: 'Research [topic] and make sure you're up to date on all capabilities, then [synthesis task]'
Custom instruction example: 'Do not put bullet points in any output. Always include warm closing. Frame answers for web design industry.'
